source_evidence: Lenders consider leveraged loans to have an above-average risk that the borrower will be unable to pay back the loan (also known as the risk of default).
question: Why do leveraged loans carry above-average default risk?
answer: They are generally made to borrowers who already have high levels of debt and/or a low credit rating, so borrowers may be less able to repay. Even when a loan is secured by collateral, that collateral may not be valuable enough to repay the lender if the borrower defaults.
